subject: Tenant Portal egress: FQDN→IP proofing & firewall rule model

From: Ava Jones <ava.jones@edgeworks.com>

Date: Tue, 14 Feb 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Tenant Portal egress: FQDN→IP proofing requirements

Hi Priyom,

Thanks for the demo last week. Our security team needs a clear approach for allowlisting private endpoint egress from Redwood's tenant portal. Two specific asks: 1) we require evidence that outbound FQDNs used by the runtime reliably resolve to a small stable set of IPs (or an accepted CDN range) for firewall rules, and 2) we need guidance for temporary/ephemeral NAT IP behavior during burst scaling so we don't break the tenant's perimeter.

Can you share a recommended proofing process, sample firewall rule snippets, and any logs or artifacts we should expect to hand back once the control plane is enabled? We prefer a template we can attach to our change request (RFC).

Appreciate a short checklist — our change window is next Thursday.

Thanks,
Ava Jones
EdgeWorks Inc — Security Ops

Subject: Re: Tenant Portal egress: FQDN→IP proofing requirements

Hi Ava — thanks for the clear list. High level approach we use for private deployments below, plus I attached a short template (egress-proofing-template.xlsx) you can drop into your RFC. Key points:

1) FQDN→IP evidence: we run a 72-hour resolution and connectivity capture from the private runtime (collector) that logs DNS A/AAAA answers, SNI hostnames, and TCP/UDP endpoints at 5-minute intervals. That produces an IP snapshot and a delta timeline — attached as edgeworks-ip-snapshot.json after you run the capture.

2) Ephemeral NAT behavior: for Dedicated/private runtime we support two patterns you can choose in the RFC: a) static egress IP binding (recommended for strict firewalls) — we reserve per-tenant NAT IP(s); b) ephemeral burst NAT where outbound IPs come from a small pool with rotation; we provide rotation windows and an audit log that ties each session to a tx-id.

3) Firewall snippets: included in fw-rule-snippets.txt (ports, FQDNs, and sample iptables-A rules). We prefer allowlisting IP ranges when possible; where FQDNs are required we recommend SNI/TLS inspection with SNI-based allowlist and mTLS for private-control-plane traffic.

Next steps: if you can run the DNS/connectivity capture during your next change window, send the snapshot back and we'll produce a signed evidence pack for your change ticket. If you'd like, we can coordinate a short live test during the window to validate connectivity.

I'll loop Laura B (networking) for the NAT binding choices and Ben for compliance evidence.

—Priyom
Priyom Das
Account Lead, Redwood Inference

Priyom — quick internal note before we sign off to EdgeWorks:

- For the static egress IP option we should confirm per-tenant quota (1–3 IPs by default) and document ROTATION SLA (30d rotation for long-lived binds only on customer request).
- For ephemeral pool option: define pool size and burst behavior. Recommend we commit to a worst-case pool size of 8 IPs for initial acceptance and provide a sample rotation manifest (timestamped).
- Evidence pack: Ben, can you prepare a compliance template that includes DNS snapshots, connection logs (TLS SNI + dest IP), and a signed hash of the snapshot files? EdgeWorks asked for an RFC artifact so we should include both raw captures and a redacted summary.

Laura — on NAT: can we include an optional TLS mTLS handshake with the control-plane as a higher-assurance path — doc notes the need for key rotation guidance and CA pinning?

Marissa
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood
From: Ava Jones <ava.jones@edgeworks.com>

Thanks — that model looks good. We've run the 72-hour capture from our staging tenant during the midday window. Summary attached (edgeworks-ip-snapshot.json). Initial observations: the runtime resolved three stable A records for control.redwood-inference.com and two ephemeral IPs for the shared blob-cdn.edgeworks.net domain during bursts.

Requesting: 1) please produce the signed evidence pack so we can attach it to our RFC, and 2) confirm whether the ephemeral CDN IPs are acceptable to our perimeter if we add an SNI-based rule (we cannot open wide ranges).

We also prefer static per-tenant egress for the control-plane; can you confirm how long the IP lease would be in that flow?

Ava

Ava — thanks for the capture and summary, good signal. Short answers and attached artifacts: fw-rule-snippets.txt (contains sample iptables and firewall ACLs), edgeworks-ip-snapshot.json (signed hash included), and the evidence pack in the shared Drive link.

- Ephemeral CDN IPs: acceptable if you use an SNI-based allowlist + TLS inspection, or if you allow the specific CDN ASN/ranges. We do not recommend opening large public ranges. We will include an explanatory note you can paste into your RFC: "For blob-cdn.edgeworks.net, expected outbound IPs may vary; recommend SNI allowlist + limited outbound port 443 to the CDN FQDNs or permit the listed ASN ranges in the attached snapshot."

- Static per-tenant egress lease: default assignment is one dedicated NAT IP with a 90-day auto-rotation unless the customer requests a fixed (non-rotating) lease; fixed leases require SOC2+ contract clause and an addendum (we've included a template clause in the Drive link). If you need 2–3 IPs for HA we can reserve them — see quota table in the template.

- What you'll get in the evidence pack: DNS A/AAAA timeline, TLS SNI sampling, connection timestamps (tx-id → source ephemeral port → dest IP), and a signed SHA256 checksum file for the artifacts. Ben will provide the compliance summary you can include in your change request.

If that all works, we can sign the pack today and I will mark the thread as "evidence provided" so you can close the RFC post-change.

—Priyom
Attachments: fw-rule-snippets.txt; egress-proofing-template.xlsx (attached in previous mail)
